title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Bill 2026
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change tax practitioner regulation, foreign resident capital gains taxation, merger controls, competition policy references and rules for charitable giving and withholding credits.
Maximum civil penalties for tax practitioner misconduct would rise to 2,500 penalty units for individuals and 50,000 for companies and significant global entities.
Certain foreign investors selling Australian renewable energy assets would receive a transitional 50 per cent capital gains tax discount for events through 30 June 2030.
changes: New criminal offences would cover unauthorised paid tax services, advertising and false claims of registration.
The Tax Practitioners Board could issue infringement notices and accept enforceable undertakings.
Completed acquisitions that should have been notified would become voidable by court order rather than automatically void.
Legislative references would be updated to the 2024 National Competition Policy Agreement.
Public and private ancillary funds would be renamed public and private giving funds.
Foreign resident capital gains withholding credits could be claimed in the transaction's income year where withholding had been paid to the Commissioner of Taxation.
summary.affected: Tax practitioners, taxpayers, foreign investors, merger parties, charities, giving funds and regulators are affected.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Speaking on the Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Bill 2026, the Nationals speaker said the Coalition would not oppose the bill in the House but wants it referred to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee, warning new capital gains tax rules on foreign investment, offset by a discount for renewable projects only, could threaten the viability of major projects like the $6 billion Karratha ammonia urea plant and a proposed oil refinery. He supported other schedules including strengthened Tax Practitioners Board penalties of up to $18 million and merger law and philanthropy provisions.

speeches.speaker: Tom French
speeches.brief: Introducing the Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Bill 2026, the speaker said it strengthens the Tax Practitioners Board's enforcement powers following the PwC leaks scandal, doubling the maximum ban period for serious misconduct from five to ten years, and clarifies foreign resident capital gains tax rules for assets connected to Australian land and resources, including a $50 million notification threshold. The bill also reforms the merger regime so unnotified transactions become voidable rather than automatically void, extends deductible gift recipient status to several charities, and originally proposed a 50 per cent capital gains tax discount for foreign renewable energy investors until 2030.
